title: The Red Build
brief: The release failed before tests even started. SHIP suggests skipping the checks. Find the actual failure, repair the artifact, then investigate what the tests reveal.
objective: Repair the build and the discount regression without bypassing tests.
hint: Read the build log first. Fix the module path and rerun. Once the build passes, inspect the test report and repair the boundary condition.
learning: Build failures and test failures are different signals. Fix the cause, keep required tests enabled, and rerun the same checks before release.

title: The Leaked Secret
brief: A fictional service credential was committed to a public repository. Deleting a line will not revoke the credential. Contain the exposure, investigate usage and history, then repair delivery.
objective: Revoke the exposed credential, assess exposure, and migrate the application to a fresh managed secret.
hint: Revoke first. Inspect audit and history evidence. Provision a replacement in the vault, switch the source to runtime injection, and add a secrets check.
learning: Revocation contains credential exposure. Rotation restores service safely. Removing hardcoding and scanning help prevention; rewriting history alone does not revoke a leaked credential.

title: Shift Left!
brief: The last release found problems only in staging. Move detection earlier and enforce it. Prove that a synthetic bad change is blocked while a clean change can still ship.
objective: Configure early checks and required gates, then exercise both bad and clean changes.
hint: Install commit and CI secret checks, require them for promotion, and run the synthetic bad change. After it is blocked, switch to the clean change and rerun.
learning: Early checks improve feedback. Local hooks can be bypassed; enforced CI gates provide an independent boundary. Test both rejection of unsafe changes and acceptance of valid work.

title: Scan Wars
brief: Two scanners disagree about a demo search endpoint. Static analysis finds an injection path and a fixture string. Dynamic analysis needs a running staging target. Use the evidence to fix the real finding without suppressing everything.
objective: Run SAST and DAST, patch the injection, and document the fixture finding using evidence.
hint: Run SAST first and inspect findings. Patch query construction and document the non-executable fixture. Deploy the isolated staging target, then run DAST against it.
learning: SAST inspects source; DAST exercises a running target. Neither proves complete security. Triage findings with evidence, narrowly document false positives, and rerun scans after changes.

title: Dependency Hell
brief: The vulnerable package is not in your direct dependencies. It arrives through a renderer. Trace the dependency graph, choose a compatible fix, and regenerate the lockfile before testing the artifact.
objective: Repair the transitive dependency, regenerate the lockfile, and verify behavior and inventory.
hint: Generate an SBOM and run SCA. Upgrade the parent renderer to the compatible patched release, regenerate the lockfile, then run regression tests and SCA again.
learning: An SBOM inventories components; SCA associates components with vulnerability information. Fix transitive dependencies through compatible parent upgrades, and verify the resolved lockfile and behavior. Packages and advisories here are fictional.

title: Permission Denied
brief: The reporting worker cannot read its own artifacts. A wildcard administrator role would unblock it, but also expose every environment. Investigate the denied operation and scope a service identity to the actual workload.
objective: Restore report delivery with a scoped service identity and prove forbidden operations remain denied.
hint: Read the access denial and identity policy. Bind the reporting identity, grant read on its own artifact prefix, and test both allowed and forbidden operations.
learning: Least privilege grants the actions and resources a workload needs. Validate positive access and negative boundaries; a successful request alone does not prove a policy is safe.

title: The Green Lie
brief: A pull request shows a green icon, yet its security workflow never ran. A path filter skipped it and promotion only checked the job name. Make skipped or missing evidence block the release.
objective: Repair workflow coverage and required-check enforcement, and test a deliberately skipped run.
hint: Inspect the workflow and promotion policy. Remove the path gap, require the completed check, then try a skipped fixture before the normal fixture.
learning: A skipped job is not evidence of a passing control. Required checks need coverage, fail-closed handling, and protection from bypass. Verify missing or skipped results as well as passing results.

title: The Compromised Build
brief: The artifact is signed, but its build originated from an unexpected repository. The signing identity alone does not establish trust. Quarantine the output and verify a rebuilt artifact against the intended source and builder.
objective: Quarantine the suspect artifact and rebuild with pinned inputs, then verify source, builder and digest.
hint: Inspect provenance first. Quarantine before rebuilding. Pin the trusted builder and inputs, rebuild from reviewed source, and verify the entire provenance tuple.
learning: A signature authenticates a signing identity; it does not guarantee trusted source or behavior. Check provenance against policy: intended source, reviewed commit, approved builder and artifact digest.

builder: approved-builder / pinned inputs
digest: demo-rebuilt-002

title: Zero-Day Friday
brief: Two findings arrive at once. One is critical in an unreachable demo tool; another is high severity in a public upload path. Determine exposure and contain the reachable route before preparing a tested permanent fix.
objective: Prioritize the reachable public upload flaw, contain it, then deploy a tested patch and remove the temporary restriction safely.
hint: Read reachability evidence. Restrict uploads first, record the lower-exposure finding for follow-up, patch the public route and test it. Only reopen uploads after the patch passes.
learning: Severity is one input to prioritization. Reachability, exposure and impact determine urgency. Temporary containment buys time but needs a tested permanent remediation and explicit removal.

title: Incident Commander
brief: The newest demo release is serving corrupted responses. Preserve evidence, contain the release and recover a known-good artifact. Restoring availability is valid containment; do not keep a harmful release live just to investigate it.
objective: Contain the incident, preserve evidence, recover the verified release and validate service health before closure.
hint: Rollback can happen immediately. Capture the synthetic incident evidence, verify a known-good artifact, restore it, fix the faulty configuration and run health checks before closure.
learning: Containment and recovery are legitimate first responses. Preserve evidence in parallel, restore a known-good state, validate behavior and add a regression gate before closing the incident.

title: Technical Debt
brief: TECH DEBT is the accumulation of shortcuts: exposed credentials, untested releases, drifting dependencies and unverified recovery. Rebuild the delivery system so the next release stays healthy under pressure.
objective: Retire four systemic shortcuts, rehearse an unsafe release, then deliver the clean release with recovery ready.
hint: Inspect the debt ledger. Replace shared secrets, enforce tests, pin patched dependencies and rehearse rollback. Require these controls, test an unsafe fixture, then ship the clean fixture.
learning: Durable improvement combines preventive controls, detection, remediation and recovery. A clean release is stronger evidence when the same system also blocks unsafe work and can recover from failure.

evidence.before:

Test promotion gate: optional
Dependency resolution: drifting
Rollback procedure: untested
Unsafe release fixture exercises all four shortcuts.

evidence.title: Release acceptance contract
evidence.before:

CLEAN: runtime binding, passing regressions, patched lockfile, verified rollback
Required: reject BAD and accept CLEAN without bypassing controls.
